bikes.summary: Testers treat this generation as the low-to-mid torque specialist of the 250F class: it pulls almost like a bigger bike out of corners and lets riders carry a higher gear, but it runs out of revs earlier than the European bikes, so it needs more shifting. The KYB spring fork is well liked, though it softens after break-in and dives on corner entry for faster or heavier riders. Off-throttle engine braking pitches the chassis, and most testers load a less-engine-braking or top-end map in the app. Recurring owner complaints are a cramped cockpit for tall riders, seat foam that packs down, a soft front brake and an air filter that does not seal well.

points.statement: Strong bottom-to-mid torque for a 250F; riders can corner a gear higher than on rival bikes.
Runs out of pull and over-rev earlier than the KTM-group and Honda bikes, so riders shift more.
The 2021-2023 engine lost a little bottom-end roll-on compared with 2019-2020 while revving more freely.
Noticeable engine braking makes the chassis pitch on corner entry at stock settings.
Stock maps feel abrupt for average riders, and a slight hesitation at the first crack of throttle in slow ruts remained even after remapping on the 2023.
The KYB spring fork is rated among the best stock forks and handles big whoops well.
Once broken in the fork goes soft and dives into flat corners and under braking for faster or heavier riders.
At about 105 mm sag the shock balances riders from roughly 150 to 195 lb with good rear traction.
The 2022 update added low-speed fork damping, giving more hold-up, less pitching and better braking-bump compliance.
Planted, predictable chassis that tracks straight and turns point-and-shoot; less agile than the KTM but forgiving, with a frame that flexes well.
Cockpit is cramped for riders around 5'10 and taller, and seat foam packs down within 10-20 hours.
Front brake feels mushy or spongy from the factory.
Air filter does not seal well; dirt collects at the back of the airbox. The 2020 filter grommet helped but did not fully cure it.
Stock muffler packing goes raspy after about 10-20 hours.
Stock lithium batteries failed on a test bike and left the tester stranded.
A few owners reported cam chain failures on 2019-2020 bikes; the sample is small.
A few owners tied hard starting, stalling and fouled plugs to the idle setting.
Cable clutch heats up under hard use and needs free play adjusted between motos.
Some bikes have too much throttle free play even with the adjuster fully out.

common_fixes.problem: Chassis pitches on corner entry from engine braking
common_fixes.fix: Load a less-engine-braking (free-revving) map in the Power Tuner app
common_fixes.result: Less decel pitching, lighter mid-corner feel and a little more top end

common_fixes.problem: Runs out of pull on top
common_fixes.fix: Tuner or factory map aimed at mid and top end
common_fixes.result: More pull through 2nd and 3rd and the next gear lands in the power; 13/51 stopped forcing short shifts

common_fixes.problem: Low-to-mid lacks punch on stock exhaust
common_fixes.fix: Full aftermarket exhaust system
common_fixes.result: More low-to-mid pull and smoother pull through the gears; top end about the same

common_fixes.fix: Vent the airbox lid (drilled holes or vented cover)
common_fixes.result: More pull and response; intake noise goes up and the filter gets dirtier faster

common_fixes.problem: Wants more top end and over-rev
common_fixes.fix: Ported head or engine kit (factory accessory kit or dual-injector setup)
common_fixes.result: Stronger top-end surge and over-rev, with slightly less low-end response on one kit

common_fixes.problem: Fork dives and front washes in flat corners
common_fixes.fix: Stiffer 4.8 N/mm fork springs or 5 cc more fork oil
common_fixes.result: More hold-up, less pitching and a calmer front under braking

common_fixes.fix: Lower and rearward footpeg mounts (about 5-7 mm down and 5 mm back)
common_fixes.result: More room for riders 5'8 to 6'2 without losing ground clearance

common_fixes.fix: Swap to an older KTM Brembo master cylinder with the stock Yamaha caliper
common_fixes.result: Firmer, more powerful front brake

disagreements.topic: Where the stock engine is strongest
sides: Most tests call it the strongest low-to-mid engine in the class
One exhaust test found stock weaker from idle to about 10,000 rpm and stronger only above that
The shock balances a wide rider weight range with good traction
Another test found the shock wallows and turned rebound in

bikes.summary: The 2024 update moved the YZ250F to a slimmer frame based on the YZ450F, with a bigger, lower airbox. Testers agree it lost low-end snap: there is a lag off the bottom and riders need clutch, while the mid and top got stronger. Tuners blame the larger airbox. The chassis turns and tips into ruts more easily but felt busier at speed, and the 2024 fork was soft and dived. The 2025 linkage and shock changes calmed it. Alternative app maps such as the factory 'Response' map are the usual way to bring back the bottom end, and the bike is loud.

points.statement: Weaker, laggy bottom end compared with 2023; slower riders need clutch to get into the power and it can bog a gear too tall.
Stronger mid and high-rpm pull with the best over-rev this engine has had; suits fast riders who keep it revved.
Tuners link the softer low end and heavier engine-braking feel to the larger, lower-velocity airbox.
Leaves a gap between 2nd and 3rd gear; needs more shifting and corner speed.
Alternative app maps (the factory 'Response' map, test-rider and tester maps) bring back low-end response; the 2025 standard map already feels like the 2024 'Response' map.
On the 2025, testers preferred the standard map; the performance map added mid and top but took away too much bottom.
Loud and raspy when revved, with intake noise from the bigger airbox.
Feels slim and light, turns and tips into ruts very easily, with more frame feedback.
The 2024 front end feels busy or twitchy on fast, rough straights, and the chassis is stiffer and less comfortable than before.
The 2024 fork is soft: it dives in corners and under braking and blows through on big hits, and the bike pitches.
The 2024 shock wallows.
The 2025 linkage and settings cut fork dive and pitching, hold the bike higher in the stroke and give a more planted rear.
Even on 2024-2026 bikes the fork reacts too quickly when loading the front in corners and the front can wash; the rear sits high for riders under about 160 lb.
Cable clutch heats up and needs free play adjusted during or between motos.
About 3 lb lighter than the 2023.
Cockpit is roomier than 2023 with a flatter seat and lower, rearward pegs, yet riders 5'10 and up still found it cramped.
The stock filter let dirt into the intake on a test bike; testers fitted an aftermarket filter and cage.
Front brake still feels spongy.
Owner reports on 2024-2025 bikes show no pattern of engine failures so far.
Stock Yamaha wheels ranked toughest of the OEM wheelsets tested.
On one tuner's dyno the 2025 was 6th of 8 for peak power and lowest for torque, with the latest torque peak; the magazine noted its part-throttle feel on track is better than the numbers suggest.

common_fixes.fix: Load the 'Response' preset or a test-rider/tester map
common_fixes.result: Low end comes back, revs can drop and 3rd works in corners; 'Response' hits a little harder

common_fixes.fix: One tooth smaller rear sprocket (50 to 49) to lengthen the gears
common_fixes.result: Helped the lull but did not fix it

common_fixes.fix: 2-3 clicks more fork compression, raise fork tubes about 2.5 mm, or a stiffer revalve
common_fixes.result: Less dive and more hold-up; one revalve for intermediate/pro riders removed wallow, though vet testers preferred stock

common_fixes.fix: Slide the fork tubes down a few millimetres in the clamps
common_fixes.result: Calmer turn-in

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket clamps at 23 mm offset (stock 22)
common_fixes.result: Calmer entry on choppy ground and less head shake; 22 mm in the aftermarket clamps gave more front traction

common_fixes.fix: Fit a 2023-24 YZ450F airbox with a remapped aftermarket ECU
common_fixes.result: Better low-end pickup and more pull through 2nd-4th; 3rd usable in corners

common_fixes.fix: Vented airbox lid
common_fixes.result: More low response and mid punch; much louder intake

common_fixes.problem: Fork too quick in corners, rear high for light riders
common_fixes.fix: Slower rebound both ends and softer shock high-speed compression for riders under 160 lb
common_fixes.result: Calmer chassis; rear squats on exits and the fork settles on braking bumps

sides: Testers found the top end strong and the best over-rev Yamaha has made on this engine
A 2024 shootout found it still could not match the KTM, Husqvarna, Kawasaki or GasGas at high rpm
Some testers found the front busy and twitchy at speed
Another test found it nimble with no stability issues
Several tests call the airbox loud
One launch tester found it quieter than before at lower revs

bikes.summary: Only launch impressions exist so far. One heavier tester found it slightly soft right off the bottom but pulling harder and longer as revs rise, turning in willingly, with stock suspension soft over braking bumps for his weight. Another tester's setting changes were aimed at bigger jump landings.

points.statement: A touch soft right off the bottom; an accessory intake and a more aggressive map sharpen it.
Pulls harder and longer as revs rise, past where riders expect the limiter.
Turns in willingly and holds lines.
Stock suspension felt soft over braking bumps for a heavier rider.

bikes.summary: Testers liked this generation's engine on the track: broad, linear power with strong pull, though the first crack of throttle can be abrupt and most testers loaded a smoother preset such as the TP map. From 2020 it felt mellower below about 9,000 rpm with lighter engine braking and a more precise chassis. The 2018-2019 felt twitchy at speed. The KYB suspension was praised for comfort across a wide rider weight range, and the cable clutch for its light pull. Recurring complaints were cramped ergonomics for tall riders, seat foam that packs down, an air filter setup that lets dirt in and slow hot restarts.

points.statement: Smooth and linear overall, but the first crack of throttle is abrupt or jerky, especially on hard-pack.
From 2020 the engine feels mellow below about 9,000 rpm and does its best work above it, with lighter engine braking so it coasts into corners.
The 2018-2019 engine had a long usable powerband with strong low end and top end and the best throttle response in its class.
On magazine dynos it often trails rivals from about 6,000 to 8,000 rpm and comes alive late, even when peak power is competitive.
Most testers run a smoother factory preset (the TP map) or a mellower custom map instead of the stock map.
Spools up fast and spins or wheelies out of hard-pack corners; mapping alone did not fix it.
The 2018-2019 felt twitchy and loose at speed and on corner exit compared with the KTM.
From 2020 the chassis feels more precise, agile and lighter, while still steering mainly from the rear.
KYB suspension is comfortable and resists bottoming across a wide rider weight range; most testers stayed close to stock.
Once broken in, the fork dives off throttle and is slightly soft on big bumps at speed.
The 2020 shock squats and sits low under throttle, with a harsh mid-stroke.
Feels heavy or vague landing into a lean compared with the KTM and Husqvarna; magazine scales put it 15-17 lb heavier than the KTM.
Cramped for tall riders, with bars high and seat low on 2018-2019 and a firm seat that packs down.
The cable clutch was rated the best non-hydraulic clutch in the class with an easy pull.
The 2018-2019 brakes had weak initial bite and then grabbed; the 2020 Nissin front is much stronger and touchier.
Air filter setup lets dirt in: the flat filter dries on the backfire screen, and without the screen dirt can drop into the boot during filter changes.
Slow hot restarts after a stall and quick overheating at idle.
One test bike went 100 hours with basic maintenance.
The wrap-around exhaust is hard to remove and intake noise is loud.
Won a 2020 450 bracket shootout and was ranked first or second by every tester in another.

common_fixes.fix: Run the smoother TP 3.0 preset or another softer factory map
common_fixes.result: Linear, easy roll-on that pulls longer; also good for starts

common_fixes.problem: Abrupt low end for experienced riders
common_fixes.fix: Ride one gear higher on the stock map
common_fixes.result: Softens the hit and engine braking and avoids stalling

common_fixes.fix: Heavier steel clutch basket
common_fixes.result: Calmer exits and less wheelspin, with slightly more engine braking

common_fixes.fix: Longer aftermarket link arm plus softer high-speed compression
common_fixes.result: Flatter decel, better exit traction; firmer if ridden lazily

common_fixes.fix: Revalve on stock springs
common_fixes.result: More fork hold-up without deflection, firmer shock that squats less

common_fixes.fix: Taller seat and lower/rearward footpegs
common_fixes.result: Better attack position and easier sit-to-stand

common_fixes.fix: Domed filter kit and raised airbox lid, optionally with a tuner map
common_fixes.result: About 2 hp more at peak and more over-rev on one magazine dyno

common_fixes.problem: Chassis unsettled on acceleration and braking
common_fixes.fix: Change gearing from 13/49 to 14/53
common_fixes.result: Chassis settles and 3rd stays usable

sides: A tester's head-to-head found it ahead of the KX450 at low, mid and top
Magazine dynos put it near the bottom of the class from 6,000 to 8,000 rpm
Most testers preferred the TP preset or a mellower map
One magazine preferred the new 2020 stock map on loose, good-traction tracks
One test found both aftermarket systems lost some over-rev against a very good stock system
Other tests found full systems smoothed roll-on and added mid and top

bikes.summary: Testers rate this engine among the strongest in the class, but the first crack of throttle is very sharp: it wheelies and breaks traction, and most testers detune it with a richer low-rpm map, a flywheel weight or a smoother exhaust. The 2023-2024 chassis turns sharper than any earlier YZ450F but gives up straight-line stability, with head shake and oversteer. The 2025 linkage and mount changes calmed it for most testers. Recurring complaints are a cable clutch that fades, a thin hard seat, dirt getting past the filter cage and a loud intake.

points.statement: Very sharp first crack of throttle: it pops out of ruts, wheelies and breaks traction; most riders need it detuned.
Very strong, linear pull through the mid and top with a long over-rev; among the most powerful engines in the class.
Testers detune it with a richer low-rpm or smoother map; a fully softened map still revs past 11,000 rpm.
The sharpest-turning YZ450F yet, feeling lighter and more agile than 2022.
Less stable at speed: aggressive turn-in, front-end oversteer and head shake, plus harshness at the edge of the tire.
The 2025 linkage, mounts and springs make it more planted and less twitchy, with less pitching.
Shock is stiff on high-speed compression relative to a softer fork; on 2023 it also sat low on big hits.
The softer 2025 fork springs suit vets and novices, but fast testers found the front too soft.
The 2023 front end is light in shallow ruts and pushes when setting up wide.
The disc-spring cable clutch fades or slips under hard use and its spring is too soft; plates last 10-12 hours for a rider who covers the clutch.
Seat is thin, domed and stiff, breaks down within about 8-10 hours, and the side panel catches boots.
Even with the lower, rearward pegs the cockpit is cramped for riders 5'10 and up.
On 2023-2024 the map button sits where the kill button gets pressed, and the throttle position causes thumb blisters.
Dirt can get past the filter cage at the front edge, and pulling the filter lets dirt drop into the intake.
Loud intake roar from the front airbox.
About 5 lb lighter than the 2022 on magazine scales.
2nd and 3rd gear are poorly spaced for some riders.
Several consumer 2025 bikes broke connecting rods.
Stock Yamaha wheels ranked toughest of the OEM wheelsets tested.

common_fixes.fix: Richer map below about 5,000 rpm, often with a 48-tooth rear sprocket
common_fixes.result: Calmer exits; taller 2nd pulls longer before 3rd

common_fixes.fix: Flywheel weight (about 80 g)
common_fixes.result: Calmer power build, more traction and better lugging without extra engine braking

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket slip-on or full exhaust
common_fixes.result: Smoother, more linear low end and better rear traction, revving out about as far as stock

common_fixes.problem: Head shake and oversteer at speed
common_fixes.fix: Slide forks down in the clamps, snug the steering stem slightly, or fit 23 mm offset clamps
common_fixes.result: Calmer steering and straighter tracking

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket engine mounts
common_fixes.result: Calmer over braking bumps and more front feel on throttle, slightly heavier turn-in

common_fixes.fix: Factory-accessory hydraulic clutch kit or an aftermarket basket and spring kit
common_fixes.result: Lighter pull, more consistent engagement and starts

common_fixes.problem: Rear squat and empty feel under load
common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket linkage with sag reset to 104-105 mm
common_fixes.result: Better rear traction and comfort

common_fixes.fix: Domed filter kit plus a vented airbox cover
common_fixes.result: Over 2 hp gained and quicker revving; much louder

sides: One review found the 2025 more planted and less twitchy at speed
A race test still found head shake at speed and tuck on entry until clamps and fork height were changed
One magazine's testers mostly chose the factory Smooth Linear map and kept it
Another found it did not tame the low end enough and built a richer custom map
One magazine went to a 48-tooth rear to soften exits
A tester went to 13/50 on deep East Coast dirt to recover 2nd and reach 3rd sooner

bikes.generation: 2026 update (intake, flywheel, hydraulic clutch, frame stiffness)
bikes.summary: Testers found the 2026 smoother, quieter and easier to ride than 2025, but it gives up some low-rpm snap and peak power and ranked mid-pack or lower on shootout dynos. Several shootouts still rated it highly because the chassis is more stable and balanced than 2023-2025 while turning precisely, although it carves deep ruts and flat turns less well than the best rivals. The fork is the main setup issue: testers found it harsh in the mid-stroke but disagreed on why. The 51-tooth stock rear sprocket makes 2nd gear very short.

points.statement: Smoother and easier to ride, with a more linear low-mid and a broader peak.
Feels more plugged up or choked down low than 2025 and gives up some peak and quick revving.
Ranked mid-pack or lower on shootout dynos (about 54-57 hp), roughly 3 hp below the 2025 on one magazine's dyno.
More engine braking than 2024-2025 makes it harder to roll corners and upsets the chassis on entry.
More stable and balanced than 2023-2025 while still turning precisely.
Slides through flat turns more than it carves; weaker in deep ruts and flat-turn traction than the best rivals.
Fork feels harsh or stiff in the mid-stroke and can overpower the shock, hurting front traction.
Shock is much better than the 2025.
The stock 51-tooth rear sprocket makes 2nd gear very short and 3rd can struggle in some corners.
The new hydraulic clutch is lighter and needs no mid-moto adjustment.
Round seat, tall feel and side panels that catch boots.
Little to no vibration; least in one 2026 shootout.
Noticeably quieter than 2023-2025.
Exposed stator wire and clutch line, and a low-pressure radiator cap.
Owners around 230 lb say it needs heavier springs.

common_fixes.fix: Go from 13/51 to 13/50
common_fixes.result: Usable 2nd for vet riders and 3rd comes in easier; fast riders kept 51

common_fixes.fix: Fit a 2025-style accessory airbox or raised intake cover with a freer aftermarket or 2025 exhaust
common_fixes.result: Stronger, more responsive feel with clearer bottom-end gain

common_fixes.fix: App map that relaxes the engine on deceleration
common_fixes.result: Better corner-entry balance

common_fixes.fix: Optional test-rider or tester maps
common_fixes.result: More low-end excitement or exit connection

sides: One shootout found it stiff early and overpowering the shock; the fix was raising the fork 2-5 mm and softening compression
A race test found it was actually too soft and riding low where damping ramps up; more shock sag plus 2 clicks stiffer fork compression made it plusher
One magazine said the new frame turns with less effort
Another shootout found it weaker carving flat turns and ruts

bikes.summary: Only one day-one magazine test so far. On paper the 2027 fork is softer, but testers found it rode higher in the stroke and harsher than the 2026, and they softened fork compression.

points.statement: Fork rides higher in the stroke and feels harsher than 2026 despite softer specs; testers went 2 clicks softer on compression, and slower riders raised the forks 5 mm.

bikes.summary: One outlet tested this generation. Testers found it strong and smooth off the bottom, hard to stall and free-revving, with a plush, stable chassis. On the 2019 the clutch lost bite on sudden release.

points.statement: Strong, smooth bottom end that is hard to stall, then lively and free-revving through the mid and top.
Plush and stable chassis.
Clutch lost bite on sudden release on the 2019 test bike.

common_fixes.fix: A little less fork compression, a little more shock high-speed compression, rear ride height kept up, one tooth smaller rear sprocket for tight going
common_fixes.result: Better balance in tight terrain

bikes.summary: Testers found this FX smooth and torquey down low, able to lug deep without much clutch and stall less than rivals, though the stock map 1 felt too aggressive and jerky off the bottom. The chassis felt more agile than the 2019-2020 but steered heavier in tight trees. Stock suspension suits slow technical terrain but is too soft for fast GP and desert racing.

points.statement: Smooth low-end torque that lugs deep with little clutch; stalls less than rivals.
Stock map 1 feels too aggressive and jerky off the bottom; testers prefer softer maps for tight terrain.
More agile and precise than 2019-2020 but with longer, heavier steering in tight trees.
Stock suspension is too soft for high-speed GP or desert racing and rides low; it works well in slow technical terrain.
About 53 hp on one magazine's dyno.

common_fixes.problem: Too soft for desert and GP
common_fixes.fix: Stiffer fork and shock springs with minor valving changes, and 14/52 gearing
common_fixes.result: Better bump absorption and bottoming resistance; chassis settles on acceleration and 2nd is usable in corners

common_fixes.fix: Softer tester-made map
common_fixes.result: Can lug with little clutch

bikes.summary: Testers agree the FX is quick and strong through the mid and top, but they disagree on the low end: one magazine called it detuned and manageable, while another found the low-rpm response crisp enough to be unsettling and tuned the maps down. First gear is so low it is rarely used. The most common chassis complaint is a lack of stability at speed, with slight head shake in chop. Opinions on the KYB suspension range from plush and predictable to stiff and race-oriented.

points.statement: First gear is extremely low and rarely used; 2nd works in tight woods and 3rd is the key gear.
Wants more stability at speed; slight head shake over high-speed chop.
Feels much lighter and more precise than earlier FX models, with a little front squirm under hard braking and less bump compliance.
KYB spring fork rated the most predictable of the off-road 450s: plush and never blows through.
A 200 lb tester found the fork soft and sometimes harsh and slowed rebound; stock springs are slightly light for that weight.
Seat shape, harsh grips and hard-to-grip sides; no stock handguards.
Cable clutch survived a 10-hour race, but testers preferred the accessory hydraulic kit.
In tight or muddy terrain testers run the mellow map with the app power slider turned down and traction control on; fast riders keep the stock map.

common_fixes.fix: Two clicks more fork compression, 23.5 mm offset clamps, or a more stretched-out setup for fast races
common_fixes.result: Head shake gone, more stability and plant; one setup turned worse when seated

common_fixes.fix: Fork 5 mm up (stock 8) with more compression, 100 mm sag, 14/52 or 14/53 gearing
common_fixes.result: More stability at speed

common_fixes.problem: Throttle jolts and stalling in tight terrain
common_fixes.fix: Factory-accessory 50 g flywheel weight
common_fixes.result: Smoother off idle and less stall risk; revs build slower, so 3rd is harder to pull for fast riders

common_fixes.fix: Foam mousse inserts
common_fixes.result: No flats in rocky races

sides: One race test called it detuned, quick-revving and manageable
Another found crisp, sometimes unsettling low-rpm response, and the 2026 stock map felt aggressive
Rated plush and the most predictable of the off-road 450s
Found stiff and race-oriented on the 2026, or soft for a 200 lb rider

bikes.summary: Testers liked the FX's strong bottom end and wide-ratio gearbox, which lets riders stay in one gear on most trails, with top-end pull close to the best 250Fs. The stock suspension suits East Coast roots and rocks but is too soft for fast GP, desert or motocross. Starting was a weak point, especially in gear or on hot restarts.

points.statement: Strong bottom end that lugs well; the wide-ratio box lets most trail be ridden in one gear.
No mid-to-top drop-off, and top-end pull close to the hardest-pulling 250F, though it is not the quickest-revving.
GNCC-style valving rolls over rocks and roots and suits East Coast woods.
Stock suspension is too soft and wallowy for fast GP, desert, motocross or aggressive riders.
Hard to start in gear and on hot restarts.
On MX or GP tracks riders hunt between 2nd-3rd and 3rd-4th.

A long-term desert bike needed throttle cables and wheel bearings around 60 hours, clutch plates at 75 and a top end with timing chain around 80; its crank later failed after engine mods and long stretches on the rev limiter.

common_fixes.fix: Stiffer springs, revalve and fork oil raised (295 cc to about 320-365 cc)
common_fixes.result: More hold-up for braking and turns, smoother bottoming, less see-saw while keeping comfort

common_fixes.problem: Gaps between gears on MX or GP
common_fixes.fix: Add 1-2 teeth to the rear sprocket
common_fixes.result: Less hunting between gears

common_fixes.fix: Start in neutral, or crack the throttle while pressing the starter
common_fixes.result: Starts reliably

bikes.summary: Mainly one outlet's first impression. Testers found strong low-end torque that lugs and recovers from too tall a gear, a strong midrange and a top end competitive with the highest-revving 250Fs. The stock fork felt firm early and rode high while the shock felt soft, so the bike was unbalanced until the clickers were reset.

points.statement: Exceptional low-end torque for a 250F that lugs and recovers from too tall a gear, with a strong mid and a competitive top end.
Fork feels firm early and rides high while the shock is soft, leaving the bike unbalanced at stock settings.
About 38 hp on one magazine's rear-wheel dyno, essentially the same as 2021.

common_fixes.fix: Soften the fork clickers and add shock high-speed compression
common_fixes.result: Balanced and raceable close to stock

bikes.summary: Testers found a longer, more linear powerband with a strong bottom-end hit, and suspension that stays plush over roots and rocks while resisting bottoming. Two separate tests reported the bike hard to start in gear even when warm.

points.statement: Hard to start in gear even when warm; riders restart in neutral.
Plush over rocks, roots and whoops yet resists bottoming at stock settings.
Longer, more linear powerband with a strong bottom-end hit.
One tester sometimes wanted a lower 1st and taller 6th.

bikes.summary: Magazine tests found the older YZ125 pulled harder than the KTM 125 below about 8,000 rpm and was easy to keep on the pipe, but fell well behind it on top. Suspension is set up for light riders.

points.statement: Pulls harder than the KTM 125 below about 8,000 rpm and is easy to keep on the pipe.
Clearly slower than the KTM 125 above about 8,000 rpm, roughly 3-4 hp down at peak.
Set up for light riders; fast or heavy riders need stiffer springs.
Stock gearing is slightly tall for a lugging style.

common_fixes.fix: 13/49 sprocket
common_fixes.result: More 2nd-gear grunt and earlier 3rd

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket pipe (about 2 hp); porting with raised compression and race gas for more
common_fixes.result: Pipe choice moves power toward the top or toward the low-mid

bikes.summary: The 2022 engine traded bottom end for more mid-to-top: testers found it weaker off the bottom and slower to come on the pipe, so riders slip the clutch out of turns, though pros liked it. On dynos it trails the European 125s. Many owners report rich jetting down low, with plug fouling and bogging, and lean it out. The suspension suits roughly 150-175 lb riders; heavier or faster riders find it soft.

points.statement: Weaker off the bottom and slower to come on the pipe than the 2021; riders slip the clutch out of turns and beginners struggle.
Stronger from about 7,500 rpm to peak than the old engine; pros liked it.
Makes the least peak power of the current 125s on magazine dynos.
Stock jetting runs rich low-to-mid: plug fouling on trails, burbling on coast-down and bogs off jump faces.
Suspension suits roughly 150-175 lb riders; heavier or faster riders find it soft, even after the 2025 spring and valving change.
The 2022 springs and valving are too stiff for riders around 155 lb and for novice or vet riders.
Stock front tire lost grip after 6-8 hours.

common_fixes.problem: Rich low end, fouling and bog
common_fixes.fix: Leaner pilot jet and a different needle (Y4 or CCL family), air screw about 1.25-1.75 turns, power jet adjusted
common_fixes.result: Cleaner low end with no bog for most owners; no single fix works for everyone

common_fixes.problem: Can't pull 3rd in deep soil or hills
common_fixes.fix: 13/50 rear sprocket
common_fixes.result: 3rd gear usable

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket pipe and silencer
common_fixes.result: No change below about 9,500 rpm, then faster build and more over-rev (about 1.4 hp on one dyno)

common_fixes.fix: Bolt-on package: pipe, ported cylinder and head, race piston, programmable ignition, reeds
common_fixes.result: Soft low end gone and strong pull into the over-rev on race fuel

sides: Dynos put it last among the current 125s
One magazine's riders still rated it strongest in the midrange, crediting its low flywheel effect

bikes.summary: The YZ250 engine has been largely unchanged since 2006. A magazine found it makes its best power higher in the revs and does not like being lugged, so riders need the clutch out of corners. The KTM 250 SX was stronger low-mid, but the Yamaha was easier to ride and kept pulling past its peak. Owners often find stock jetting rich down low.

points.statement: Doesn't like being lugged and needs clutch out of corners; the KTM 250 SX is about 4 hp stronger around 7,000 rpm.
Keeps pulling past its peak and is easier to ride than the KTM.
Stock pilot runs rich at the bottom near sea level.

common_fixes.fix: Leaner pilot (about 45-48) and smaller power jet, needle clip adjusted
common_fixes.result: Cleaner low end; one trail rider stopped fouling plugs

common_fixes.fix: Re-time the power-valve governor by changing thrust washers so the valve opens earlier
common_fixes.result: Fills the dip; needs a leaner power jet

common_fixes.fix: Aftermarket pipe
common_fixes.result: About 2.5 hp more, mostly mid and up; too strong a hit for some vets on hard-pack

bikes.summary: Testers describe a clean bottom and a hard-hitting midrange that needs a careful throttle into turns, pulling steadily to about 8,800 rpm. Lighter, slower and older riders found the stiffer 2022-on suspension harsh, while heavier riders found the stock springs light. The fork dives and pitches after break-in. Owners commonly lean out the jetting and tighten the head's squish.

points.statement: Clean off idle with a hard-hitting midrange that needs careful throttle into turns; easy to keep in the meat, while the KTM is stronger low-mid but signs off sooner.
Stock springs are light for riders over about 155-170 lb.
The stiffer 2022-on valving feels harsh for vets, novices and light riders.
After break-in the fork dives under hard braking and pitches the bike forward.
The KYB setup has enough hold-up yet absorbs small bumps and feels balanced for an average rider.
About 217 lb without fuel, roughly 10 lb lighter than a YZ250F.
The rear-facing airbox scoops let water in when washing, and the 22 mm swingarm axle limits wheel swaps.
Owners often find stock jetting rich, even at the magazine's recommended settings.

common_fixes.problem: Springs too light for heavier riders
common_fixes.fix: Stiffer springs (about 4.6 N/mm fork, 52 N/mm shock) or a respring with revalve
common_fixes.result: One revalve fixed a fast-moving, knifing front and harsh mid-stroke while staying plush

common_fixes.problem: Fork dives and pitches after break-in
common_fixes.fix: Close up fork compression and rebound
common_fixes.result: More hold-up

common_fixes.fix: Leaner pilot, smaller power jet and needle clip changes
common_fixes.result: Cleaner running; adjust for season

common_fixes.fix: Longer silencer, milder head insert, a few degrees of ignition retard, earlier power-valve spring or a flywheel weight
common_fixes.result: More linear delivery; power-valve damper results were mixed

common_fixes.fix: Mill the head to tighten squish to about 0.045 in on pump fuel
common_fixes.result: Sharper running; head dowel bores may need deepening

common_fixes.fix: Raise needle one clip and drop the main one size
common_fixes.result: Correct jetting with the pipe

sides: A magazine found it hits harder than the KTM in the midrange
Another tester found it smooth and manageable rather than abrupt

bikes.summary: Testers found the X much more tractable than the YZ125, smooth and torquey down low for a 125, which helps in tight woods. The top end is slower-revving and down on the European 125s. The soft cross-country suspension is plush on small hits but bottoms on big motocross impacts for heavier or faster riders. The small tank and lack of skid plate and handguards were the main practical complaints.

points.statement: Smooth, controllable bottom end that lugs well for a 125; easier to recover from too tall a gear.
Slower-revving and signs off early on top; clearly down on the Husqvarna TC125.
Soft cross-country settings bottom on big MX-style hits for heavier or faster riders; one tester called it badly undersprung at 190 lb.
Small tank gives roughly 40 minutes of hard riding.
No skid plate or handguards; motocross tires work poorly off-road and vice versa.
Front brake is only average.
45 hours of riding with only routine maintenance; the cable clutch held up.

common_fixes.problem: Front vague in chop and tight turns
common_fixes.fix: Reduce race sag from about 110 mm to 107 mm
common_fixes.result: More front traction in tight turns

common_fixes.fix: Stiffer clickers and 10 cc more fork oil, or respring and revalve
common_fixes.result: Better hold-up; heavier riders still need springs

common_fixes.fix: Oversize rotor and braided line
common_fixes.result: Stronger front brake

bikes.summary: Testers found the second-generation X surprisingly torquey for a 125. It has much more low end than the 2022-on YZ125 and less engine braking, but a weaker top end. The soft suspension soaks up rocks and roots, while heavier or faster riders may want it stiffer. There is still no electric start and the tank is small.

points.statement: Surprisingly torquey; it can lug a taller gear and has much more low end than the motocross YZ125.
Weaker top end; slower than the YZ125.
Softer KYB settings absorb repeated rock, root and braking-bump hits; heavier or faster riders may want it stiffer.
No electric start and a small 1.8 gal tank that limits range.

common_fixes.fix: Leaner pilot with a different needle and slide cutaway
common_fixes.result: Cleaner running at race pace

bikes.summary: Mainly one magazine's race test plus owner reports. The X is milder and more tractable than the YZ250, with a perky low-to-mid that suits rocky, tight terrain, but it does not make more power than the YZ250 anywhere. On a motocross track the tall 4th and 5th gears leave gaps, and the soft suspension bottoms on big jumps. Owners note it often finds neutral on 2-to-1 downshifts.

points.statement: Milder and more tractable than the YZ250 with a perky low-to-mid for rocky, tight terrain; it never out-powers the YZ250.
Tall 4th and 5th leave big gaps on a motocross track.
Soft suspension rides low and bottoms on big jumps for fast riders.
Small tank and short reserve, no handguards or skid plate, kick start only.
Downshifting from 2nd to 1st on the move often finds neutral.
Testers liked stiffer clutch springs better than the softer stock ones.

common_fixes.problem: Stalling and hard hits in tight terrain
common_fixes.fix: Heavier flywheel, auto-clutch, revalve and respring, 13/51 gearing
common_fixes.result: Easier trail manners; owners call the carb simple once set up

bikes.summary: One outlet's test. The newer intake reduced the on/off feel at the bottom and mid while keeping the two-stroke rush on top. The soft suspension worked in the woods and on an MX track without bottoming.

points.statement: Smooth, strong low end with less on/off feel, but still revs out like a 250 two-stroke.
Softer than the YZ250 and absorbs roots and acceleration bumps without bottoming; go stiffer for fast western terrain.

bikes.summary: Little tester feedback exists for these years. The US bike ships restricted, and owners uncork it. Tall stock gearing made 2nd hard to hold in slow corners on one test bike.

points.statement: About 3 hp less than the YZ250F on the same magazine dyno in US form.

common_fixes.fix: Remove throttle stop, muffler restrictor and intake restrictor; pair with the competition ECU and a little more fuel if the tailpipe comes out
common_fixes.result: Engine runs closer to YZ-FX output

common_fixes.problem: 2nd gear runs out in slow corners
common_fixes.fix: 13/48 instead of 13/50 plus a slip-on and header
common_fixes.result: Holds 2nd through slow corners; sharper response but less grip in slick going

bikes.summary: One European test. Testers found the 2022 stronger across the range, especially mid to top where it revs freely. Stalling and slow hot restarts were still a trait. The small oil capacity calls for frequent oil changes.

points.statement: Stronger across the range, especially mid to top, revving freely so gears can be held longer.
Still stalls more readily than a two-stroke in technical going, and hot restarts are awkward; a softer map reduces stalling.
Small engine oil capacity, so testers advise frequent changes.

common_fixes.fix: Remove throttle stop and restrictors and fit the competition ECU
common_fixes.result: Stronger running; the ECU alone did not change off-idle response

bikes.summary: Testers found the 2025 lively, with a bigger midrange kick and a smooth climb to a high rev limit. The softer handlebar map tames it. The KYB suspension splits opinion: firm and precise at speed, but stiff on slow technical trails for some, while a 90 kg rider rated it excellent without changes. It is still a little easy to stall, and hot restarts can be slow.

points.statement: Lively, with a bigger midrange kick than before and smooth all the way to a high rev limit.
Fork feels stiff on slow technical trails, though firm and precise at speed.
Fork transmits jolts through the arms over bigger chop for fast riders.
A little easy to stall, and hot restarts can take several seconds, worse after a stall on a hill.
Six-speed spread works from tight singletrack to fire roads.
The linkage collects dirt, and the right-side axle marks are hidden, so align the wheel from the left.

common_fixes.fix: Run less race sag than usual (about 95-100 mm)
common_fixes.result: Better-balanced chassis

common_fixes.fix: Use the softer second map
common_fixes.result: Flatter midrange with some traction-control effect

sides: Firm or stiff on slow technical trails
A 90 kg tester rated it a standout with no changes on grass track, enduro loops and trails

bikes.summary: In US form testers found the WR450F docile and torquey, great on slow, tight trails but short of punch in sand, hills and open terrain. Uncorking it and fitting the competition ECU transforms it to near-YZ450FX performance. The trail-valved suspension is soft early and progressive deeper and needs firming up for fast desert. Unrestricted Australian bikes felt the opposite, too aggressive on hard-pack.

points.statement: US-spec bike is docile and torquey with no real 450 hit; great on tight trails but struggles in sand, hills and open terrain.
Same KYB hardware as the FX with softer trail valving: soft early, progressive deeper; firm it up for fast desert.
Stock bikes can stumble, cough or die when leaned over at low rpm.
Fuel range is far below claims when ridden hard; one test ran dry at 35 miles in sand.
Australian-spec 2019 felt too aggressive and tiring on hard-pack and rocks; the handlebar soft map did not calm it enough.

common_fixes.fix: Remove throttle stop and intake/muffler restrictors and install the competition ECU, optionally with a slip-on
common_fixes.result: Engine package close to the YZ450FX; one magazine estimated almost 20 hp more

common_fixes.fix: Remap through the communication unit
common_fixes.result: Cured, even with the stock quiet pipe

common_fixes.fix: Softer app maps
common_fixes.result: Far less aggressive in tight terrain

sides: One test found the stock bike stumbling and dying at low rpm when leaned over
Another 2021 test reported no stalling

bikes.summary: Testers find the newer WR450F punchy and willing to rev, with a very low first gear and enough torque in 2nd and 3rd to pull out of corners with little clutch. The app and mellow map can tame it a lot. Stock suspension felt firm at slow pace, so testers softened it with the fork knobs. The flameout trait of older WRs is mostly gone.

points.statement: Punchy and willing to rev from mid to top with good low-speed traction; the app and mellow map tame it for slick going or beginners.
Stock suspension feels firm at slow pace; testers softened compression.
Flameout is mostly gone, but bogging it in too high a gear can still make it sputter.
Tall seat.
Clutch pull felt heavy at first; moving the perch outward helped.

common_fixes.fix: Start on the mellow map and switch to full power as the ground dries
common_fixes.result: Better traction
